'''Robert Vita Kohn''' (October 5, 1953 – January 12, 2026) was an American mathematician who worked on [[partial differential equations]], [[calculus of variations]], mathematical [[materials science]] and [[mathematical finance]]. He was a professor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], [[New York University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=2JYb4lkAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Google Scholar|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

== Background ==
Kohn studied mathematics at [[Harvard University]], obtaining his bachelor's degree in 1974. He obtained his Ph.D. at [[Princeton University]] in 1979, as a student of [[Frederick Almgren]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy | id= 17379 | name= Robert Vita Kohn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://math.nyu.edu/faculty/kohn/cv-sept2015.pdf|title=Robert V. Kohn CV}}</ref>

Kohn died of cancer on January 12, 2026, at the age of 72.<ref>[https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1498/ Professor Emeritus Robert Kohn (1953–2026)]</ref>

== Work ==
Kohn is best known for his work on [[Partial differential equation|non-linear partial differential equations]], including work with [[Louis Nirenberg]] and [[Luis Caffarelli]] in which they obtained partial results about the regularity of weak solutions of the [[Navier–Stokes equations]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Catrina |first=Florin |last2=Wang |first2=Zhi-Qiang |title=On the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg Inequalities: Sharp Constants, Existence (and Nonexistence), and Symmetry of Extremal Functions |url=https://www.usu.edu/math/wang/cpam.pdf}}</ref>

== Honors==
Kohn received a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/past-fellows/?tx_sloangrants_sloanfellows%5Baction%5D=list&tx_sloangrants_sloanfellows%5Bcontroller%5D=Fellows&cHash=8f53adde7b4458aff6de5c2679773fee |title=Sloan Foundation |access-date=2015-11-06 |archive-date=2016-10-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022115730/http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/past-fellows/?tx_sloangrants_sloanfellows&#91;action&#93;=list&tx_sloangrants_sloanfellows&#91;controller&#93;=Fellows&cHash=8f53adde7b4458aff6de5c2679773fee |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2006, he was a plenary speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], in Madrid (''Energy driven pattern formation'').<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |title=International Mathematical Union web-site |access-date=2015-11-06 |archive-date=2017-11-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a member of the inaugural class of Fellows of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows Directory {{!}} SIAM |url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/fellows-program/fellows-directory/ |access-date=2026-01-12 |website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |language=en-US}}</ref>. He was a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi|title=AMS :: Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|website=www.ams.org}}</ref> He was an elected member of [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/robert-v-kohn|title=Robert V. Kohn &#124; American Academy of Arts and Sciences|date=July 1, 2025|website=www.amacad.org}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
*with [[Luis Caffarelli|L. Caffarelli]] and [[Louis Nirenberg|L. Nirenberg]]: "Partial regularity of suitable weak solutions of the Navier–Stokes equations", ''[[Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics]]'', n. 35 i. 6, pp.&nbsp;771–831.
*with L. Caffarelli and L. Nirenberg, "First order interpolation inequalities with weights", ''[[Compositio Mathematica]]'' n. 53 i. 3, pp.&nbsp;259–275.
*with [[Gilbert Strang]], "Optimal design and relaxation of variational problems, I", ''Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics'', n. 39 i. 1, pp.&nbsp;113–137.
